name: AI-Powered Emissions Reporting with MOVESAI
tagline: AI and machine-learning systems that reproduce EPA's MOVES emissions simulator behind fast APIs and dashboards — so any city can estimate and report its transportation emissions online. Consolidates the former MOVESAI and Climate Action in Transportation (CAT) projects.
body: Transportation is a top source of greenhouse gases and air pollution, but the models that estimate it are slow and hard for local agencies to use. You'll build AI and machine-learning systems that reproduce EPA's MOVES emissions simulator and serve it through fast APIs and dashboards — so cities can estimate and report their transportation emissions online without running the full model. Work spans machine learning, API design, front-end dashboards, and the report that ships with it.
question: Can AI reproduce a heavyweight EPA emissions model fast enough for any city to use online?

name: Urban Air Quality & Traffic Systems with CIVIC
tagline: The data systems behind CIVIC — integrating air quality, transit, and traffic data from cities like NYC, London, and Stockholm to measure how transportation policy reshapes pollution and mobility.
body: When a city changes how people move — congestion pricing, new transit, road redesigns — does the air actually get cleaner, and for whom? You'll build the data systems behind CIVIC: integrating air quality, transit, and traffic data from cities like NYC, London, and Stockholm, then using causal inference to measure how policies shift pollution and travel. Work spans data engineering, panel databases, statistics, and communicating results to a policy audience.
question: When a city charges drivers to enter its core, does the air actually get cleaner — and who benefits?

name: Social Infrastructure & Emergency Mobility
tagline: Spatial pipelines that score civic spaces — parks, libraries, places of worship — across US cities, then link those scores to evacuation behavior and hazard exposure.
body: Cities with denser social infrastructure — parks, libraries, places of worship — tend to recover faster from disasters, but how much and where? You'll build spatial pipelines that score civic spaces across dozens of US cities, then link those scores to evacuation behavior and hazard exposure using mobility data. Work spans GIS and spatial statistics, a dashboard and API to share results, and a report connecting community infrastructure to emergency preparedness.
question: Does where your neighbors gather predict how well your city survives a disaster?

name: Bikeshare Network Analytics
tagline: One unified trip database spanning every major US bikeshare system — Bluebikes, Citi Bike, Divvy, Capital Bikeshare — modeled as mobility networks.
body: Every major US city runs a bikeshare system — Bluebikes, Citi Bike, Divvy, Capital Bikeshare — each logging millions of trips. You'll fetch and unify those records into one analysis-ready database with a shared schema, then model the resulting mobility networks to study ridership, equity, and rider behavior no single city's data can reveal alone. Work spans network science, large-scale data fetching, and database design.
question: What patterns emerge when we can compare how riders move across every major US bikeshare system?

name: Agentic Fault Tree Analysis with FaultDB
tagline: A browser platform pairing an R analysis engine with a React diagram editor — now adding agentic AI workflows for building fault and attack trees.
body: Reliability engineers spend too long fighting clunky desktop tools to answer one question: how likely is this system to fail, and which parts matter most? You'll extend FaultDB — a browser platform pairing an R analysis engine with a React diagram editor — and add agentic AI workflows that help users build fault and attack trees, run cut-set analysis, and interpret the results. Work spans LLM agent design, reliability modeling, interactive front-ends, and the API behind them.
question: What is the probability that this system fails — and which components matter most?

name: Open-Source Radiation Monitoring with SAFECAST
tagline: A new collaboration with SAFECAST, the Tokyo-based citizen-science nonprofit running the world's largest open dataset of background-radiation measurements.
body: SAFECAST is a Tokyo-based nonprofit that, after the 2011 Fukushima disaster, built the largest open dataset of background-radiation measurements — crowdsourced by citizens using handheld and fixed sensors, and released freely to the public. Today their network maps Fukushima, Ukraine, and cities worldwide to support crisis tracking and recovery in radiation-affected areas. In this new collaboration, your team will help SAFECAST build out the dashboard systems and AI integration behind their global sensor network so it can communicate accurate, impartial radiation information to the public when it matters most. We're recruiting students with skills in any of these areas: databases, sensors, APIs, React, dashboards, and data visualization — and you'll ship a working tool plus a report.
question: After a nuclear disaster, can an open citizen-run sensor network tell people what's safe — clearly, and in real time?

name: Climate Action in Transportation (CAT)
tagline: A platform that turns EPA MOVES into a public tool for estimating local transportation emissions.
body: Lead developer on Cornell's effort (with Dr. Oliver Gao) making EPA MOVES usable as a public emissions tool — dashboards, APIs, and data behind it.

name: CIVIC
tagline: A city-scale platform measuring how congestion pricing, transit, and road policy reshape air quality and mobility worldwide.
body: Causal inference on multi-city air, transit, and traffic data to test whether transportation policies actually cut pollution — and for whom.

name: Social Infrastructure Mapping
tagline: Mapping community spaces that build social capital — across Boston, Fukuoka, and the 25 largest US cities.
body: Mapping community spaces (parks, libraries, places of worship) across US cities with the Places API, then linking them to mobility and resilience outcomes.

name: Evacuation with Mobility Data
tagline: Estimating evacuation from hurricanes, wildfires, earthquakes, and floods using anonymized cell-phone movement data.
body: Using anonymized mobility data to measure who evacuates — and where they go — during hurricanes, wildfires, earthquakes, and floods.
